text: The claude-code e2e background-task scenario runs a wake-up matrix — {backgrounded bash, subagents} × {one-shot, streaming} — against a live model and asserts, in every cell, that task frames route to the right event family, that the run does not end at the first `result` but continues through the completion event and a continuation turn to `done`, that the control channel survives the held `result`, and that a healthy run ends **silently**: the hold cap is never hit — no `AdapterBackgroundHoldExpiredError` and no terminal `error` event, the run's last event being its `result` — with the absence of any hold-bound `warning` kept beside it only as a regression guard against the warning-and-carry-on shape this bound replaced.
title: The claude-code e2e background-tasks scenario runs a wake-up matrix over {backgrounded bash, subagents} × {one-shot, streaming} and asserts routing, push resume, the hold, and silence.
